content.thinking:
I need to write the entire file carefully in one pass without testing, so I'm planning out the imports and structure I'll need—pulling in the builder, THREE, texture/paint utilities, math helpers, and the toon shading kit—while trying to recall the exact API shape for how samples typically export and build their scene objects.

I'm sketching the biplane's whimsical proportions—chubby fuselage, oversized cowling and propeller, fat wheels, candy red and cream color scheme with striped wings—and working out the coordinate layout (nose, tail, wheel height, fuselage center). I'm also designing the fuselage as a loft through several stations from tail to nose, each with position, width, and height, and thinking through how to paint the surface with simple positional color logic to get the cream cowling band and tail stripe effect using the cel shading wrapper.

Now I'm working out the wing geometry: flat rounded-rectangle slabs extruded with slight thickness and bevel, positioned above the fuselage with specific spans, chords, and placement offsets for the upper wing.

I'm also adding paint detail with stripe bands near the wingtips and a small whimsical flower-style emblem decal placed as a thin plane just above the wing surface, oriented to face upward.

Now I'm positioning the lower wing, fuselage, and upper wing so they intersect correctly with the cabane struts connecting fuselage top to the upper wing, and I'm working out the interplane strut placement between the wings on both sides.

I'm adding diagonal rigging wires and shaping the engine cowling as a lathed profile around the fuselage axis, defining the radius and height points for the cowl's curved outline.

Now I'm placing exhaust pipes, the propeller hub sphere, and sketching the propeller blades as extruded outlines pointing outward with tapered width along their length.

Adjusting blade tilt angles and tip coloring, then positioning the propeller center and checking radius against floor clearance so blades don't clip through the ground—tweaking to 1.05 for a small gap. Also placing a spinner cone at the hub.

Now I'm designing the cockpits: fake open-cockpit cutouts using dark cylinders with rim torus coaming to suggest the leather lip, plus a cheerful pilot figure with goggles and a streaming scarf for whimsy, working out the loft station heights to position the pilot's head correctly above the fuselage.

Adding a whimsical plush bear passenger in the front cockpit, checking that its head and the pilot's helmet clear the upper wing properly, and repositioning the cockpits so the bear sits under the wing's center cut-out. Now I'm sketching the tail fin's side-view outline for extrusion.

I'll give the rudder playful paint stripes using sun-like bands of yellow, red, and teal based on position. Now I'm setting up the horizontal stabilizer extrusion, computing the thickness direction as the cross product of the x and y extrude axes.

Still working out the wing and stabilizer geometry...

Checking that the stabilizer doesn't extend past the tapered fuselage end—I need to adjust the fuselage tail to terminate further back so the fin and stabilizer fit properly within the tail section.

Switching to a small whimsical tail wheel instead of a skid: a thin strut dropping from the fuselage to a torus-style wheel with dark tire and cream hub, positioned so its bottom touches the ground.

For the main gear I'm sizing the wheels (~0.48 radius) using a torus shaped as a tire with a cream-and-red hubcap disc at center, then planning V-struts connecting them up to the fuselage.

Adding diagonal flying wires between the strut bays to brace the biplane structure, then working out the wing mounting heights and strut rod positions between the lower and upper wings.

Now I'm designing the wing paint scheme with rib lines and tip stripes, planning separate paint functions for the upper and lower wing surfaces using a bright red, cream, and teal color palette.

For the fuselage, I'm sketching a countershading approach using the surface normal's vertical component to split red on top from cream on the belly, plus adding a teal band and scalloped accent near the tail.

Adding panel lines and rivet details...

Continuing the station, I'm finishing the fuselage profile toward the nose and checking the cowling fits chubbily around it without clipping the gear or wheels. I'm also working out where the pilot coaming and cockpit tops line up by interpolating between stations, settling on roughly 1.69-1.71 for the cockpit disc heights.

Now I'm adding the coaming as a brown leather torus around each cockpit opening, plus small tilted windscreen panes placed in front of each seat—pilot's screen further back and lower, bear's screen forward and slightly higher—with light teal glass and thin frames to match where their heads will sit.

I'm figuring out the pilot figure: a scaled sphere for the jacketed torso, a skin-toned head sphere, and a brown leather helmet using a partial sphere so it caps the head realistically, tilted back slightly, with small ear flap spheres and goggle lenses built from short cylinders.

Working out the goggle straps as a torus wrapped around the head, plus tiny nose and mustache spheres, and sketching a scarf as a Catmull-Rom curve sweeping back from the neck to suggest it streaming in the wind.

Still shaping scarf geometry...

I realize the scarf's z-extent overlaps the tail fin, so I'm shortening its end point to avoid the collision. Then for the pilot's arms, I'm sketching brown capsule rods from the shoulders down to glove spheres gripping a control stick, though I may skip detailing the arms since they'll be hidden.

Now I'm focused on the bear sitting in the front cockpit, building the head with a tan sphere, two ear spheres with pink insets, a cream muzzle oriented toward +z, bead eyes, and a torso sphere, keeping it simple with just a red bow rather than goggles or a cap. Then I'm moving to the engine cowling, adding a lathed cream front ring and placing seven small cylinder-head bumps around the hub to suggest the radial engine.

Adding exhaust pipes and cowl paint details...

Defining the lathe profile for the nose cone shape using a set of radius/height points along the axis, keeping it to 8 points with smoothing to avoid geometry glitches.

I'll skip the gravity tank detail and simplify to cabane struts instead. For decals, I'm placing SVG flower/star emblems on the upper wing surfaces using a radial texture with teal, cream, and yellow rings.

Still placing decals...

I'm also thinking about adding small decorative pennant flags on poles at the wingtip struts, extruding little triangular flag shapes pointing backward from rods rising above the wingtip positions, which requires working out the orientation vectors so the flags sit correctly in 3D space.

I'm also planning glowing wingtip navigation lights -- red on the left side, green on the right, following standard aviation convention -- as tiny spheres positioned near the wingtips, and considering whether to add any other whimsical touches like a small mail sack strapped to the fuselage.

Now I'm adding a mail sack to the rear deck behind the cockpit as a small cream-brown sack with a knotted top, plus a rounded turtledeck fairing just behind the pilot's headrest for a bit of character.

Next I'm thinking about adding dark walkway pads near the wing roots where the lower wing meets the fuselage, plus leading-edge tape detailing and aileron outline lines on the trailing portions of both wings, and I'm sketching out a wing-paint helper function to generate these markings procedurally based on span and chord position.

Adding aileron outline detail...

For tires and hubs I'm picking dark fabric tones for the tread and cream for the hub centers, then thinking through a simple pinwheel decal plane for the wheel cover geometry and its offset position along the axle.

Now I'm working out the correct rotation axes for the torus and cylinders so they align along the x-axis as intended, then sketching the SVG spoke pattern for the decal texture.

Designing the wing emblem with a teal-cream circular badge, a yellow star, and red center, plus a fuselage side badge with a bold "7" in red on a cream circle — defining the exact shapes, colors, and text positioning for each SVG.

I'm adding a propeller hub ring, exhaust pipes along the fuselage, and considering whimsical touches like rosy cheeks while checking that the overall proportions — oversized wheels, stubby fuselage, rounded cowl — keep the total length, wingspan, and height realistic for a charming biplane.

With around 150 parts, I'm adding finer details like cowl rivets, painted fuselage seam lines, and stitched leather coaming, plus wing-root fairings and tail brace wires connecting the stabilizer tips to the fin top, along with diagonal struts bracing the stabilizer underside to the fuselage.

Merging rivet spheres into rings...

Now I'm sketching helper functions for the builder — a part-creation wrapper that takes geometry, color, position, and options, importing the proper ColorInput/Paint and PartOptions types to keep things consistent.

I'm defining color constants using cel() for a shaded palette, then starting the fuselage loft with a hull paint function that varies color by position, like switching to a cream tone near the belly.

Still writing shader zigzag logic...

Now I'm sketching the bear figure sitting in the cockpit, with a head sphere, torso dimensions, lens glass color, and brass trim colors defined.

Still placing bear facial features...

I'm positioning the muzzle, nose, eyes, and ears on the bear, checking that the ear top doesn't collide with the wing, then sketching the pilot's head and helmet position relative to the cockpit opening before moving on to the pilot's torso and arms.

Now I'm working through the arms as rods with glove spheres, then placing the tail wheel geometry—strut, torus tire, and hub—and starting on the propeller blade orientation math.

Still writing propeller code...

Finishing up the wing outline points, confirming the vertex order is consistent front-to-back. Now I'm checking how the lower wing sits against the fuselage, then moving to placing emblem decals on the fuselage using plane geometry with orientation vectors to control facing direction.

Now I'm figuring out the rudder paint banding: based on the position along the fin, I'm computing stripe colors by dividing height into bands cycling through red, cream, and teal.

For the stabilizer paint, tips get teal while the rest stays red, keeping the scheme consistent. Then I need to write out the full build, making sure I only import the types I actually use (V3, ColorInput for Paint) and avoid leaving unused imports. I'm also setting up loops to place the wing struts symmetrically on both sides at a couple of positions and heights, generating rod geometry between paired points.

I'm adding brass ferrule spheres at the strut ends, thin ink-colored wire rods for rigging, thicker cabane struts, colored navigation lights (green on one wing, red on the other) with a glow effect, and decal textures for the wheel hubs.

Now I'm placing the fuselage badge decal and checking its alignment against the fuselage width at that station to make sure it sits flush on the surface.

I'm shifting to the wheel assembly, building the hub cylinder and tire torus geometries with rotations to orient them correctly at the wheel's center position.

Skipping the fender for now and moving to write a helper function for ring-arranged rivets by z-position, radius, and count.
